report:
Conclusion: The difference looks like a small, distributed bias toward producing identity/echo continuations — i.e., Model B is slightly more “copy/echo”-prone than Model A.

Why I think this
- Patchscope readouts (layers 12, 18, 24) all produce very similar outputs that echo the input (e.g. "good cat -> good cat", "cat -> cat", "hello -> hello", numeric echoes). Injecting the difference vector consistently pushes the model to repeat/reflect tokens from the prompt.
- The logit-lens top tokens are common short/function tokens (' o', 'is', 'it', ' p', ' t', '\n', 'in', ' a', 'or', ' s'), i.e. high-frequency tokens that plausibly support copying/short echo-like continuations.
- The signal is not concentrated in a single layer/position (the norm table shows effectively zero at the reported precision), which fits a small, distributed residual-stream shift rather than a localized head or layer change.

Caveats
- The per-(layer,position) L2 norms are reported as zero (probably rounded), so the magnitude is small; this is a subtle, distributed effect rather than a large, localized change.
- I cannot name a specific training objective or mechanism from this evidence alone — only the observable behavioral bias (increased tendency to echo/copy).
